title: Check your understanding: Dataset Foundations & Quality Cascades

items.prompt: Which statement best describes a dataset from a statistical learning perspective?
choices: Any uncurated dump of server logs or raw packet captures
A curated empirical sample drawn from an unobservable joint probability distribution, serving as input to modeling or analysis
Only flat CSV files containing numeric continuous columns
A frozen checkpoint of neural network weights after optimization
items.explain: A dataset is a curated collection of observations drawn from a joint probability measure P(X, Y), structured with defined schema and scope for downstream analysis.

items.prompt: Across database systems and machine learning pipelines, how do records and attributes correspond?
choices: Records correspond to vertical features; attributes correspond to horizontal rows
Records correspond to horizontal observations (tuples/instances); attributes correspond to vertical fields (columns/covariates)
Both terms refer strictly to document-level metadata
Records are only used for text; attributes are only used for tabular data
items.explain: Records (rows/tuples/instances) represent individual observations, while attributes (columns/fields/features) represent properties measured across those observations.

items.prompt: What is the core principle of the Data-Centric AI paradigm as formulated by researchers like Andrew Ng and Sambasivan et al.?
choices: Keep the dataset fixed as an immutable benchmark while continuously expanding model parameters and layers
Hold the machine learning model architecture fixed while systematically auditing, versioning, and sanitizing the underlying dataset
Discard structured tabular schemas in favor of raw unindexed text files
Train models exclusively on synthetic noise to maximize parameter regularization
items.explain: Data-Centric AI shifts engineering effort from tweaking model architectures to rigorously auditing, sanitizing, and improving data quality.

items.prompt: The Law of Data Quality Cascades implies that early data collection and sensor errors remain isolated and can easily be fixed by scaling downstream neural network depth.
items.explain: Data quality cascades compound non-linearly across downstream preprocessing, annotation, and model optimization stages, often causing catastrophic production failures.

items.prompt: Why did the sepsis detection model trained on MIMIC ICU data collapse when deployed to an external hospital?
items.rubric: Learned nurse recording frequency (operational artifact) as a proxy for illness severity rather than genuine physiological disease biomarkers.
items.sample_answer: The model learned spurious operational correlations—specifically that bedside nurses recorded vitals more frequently when patients were crashing—rather than genuine clinical biomarkers.
